key_insight: Attention sink locations in Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) shift substantially across denoising timesteps, so pruning heuristics that preserve static attention 'sinks' (inherited from autoregressive LLMs) are suboptimal. A sink-aware pruning criterion that aggregates per-timestep importance yields much more efficient pruning without degrading generation quality.
problem_solved: Reduces inference cost of iterative denoising in DLMs by replacing AR-derived, sink-preserving pruning heuristics with a principled method that accounts for temporal variability of attention sinks.
method: Measure attention-sink behavior across the full denoising trajectory and quantify sink stability/variance per token, head, and layer.

Compute a sink-aware importance score that aggregates per-timestep attention contributions and variability, prioritizing components that are consistently important across timesteps or crucial at specific phases.
Prune parameters (e.g., heads, MLP channels) using the sink-aware score and fine-tune to recover any lost performance, comparing trade-offs against AR-style baselines.
impact: Enables more effective, model-specific pruning for DLMs, lowering FLOPs and latency for diffusion-based text generation while retaining quality—important for deploying DLMs in resource-constrained settings.
visual_elements: Timeline heatmap showing dominant attention-sink positions shifting across denoising timesteps (illustrates instability vs AR assumption).
Before/after trade-off chart (FLOPs or latency on x-axis vs generation quality on y-axis) comparing sink-aware pruning to AR-inspired baselines.
Pipeline schematic: compute per-step attention → aggregate sink-aware importance → prune → fine-tune (icons for attention map, scoring, pruning scissors, retraining).
Layer/head importance bar chart highlighting components kept vs removed under sink-aware scoring.
paper_title: Sink-Aware Pruning for Diffusion Language Models
paper_authors: Aidar Myrzakhan, Tianyi Li, Bowei Guo, Shengkun Tang, Zhiqiang Shen
